questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was in Taiwan, I am very interested in Taiwan, and I wanted to improve my mandarin proficiency.  National Taiwan University is considered as the best Uni in the Country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Course selection proces very complicated and very unsuited for exchange students. Not a good part of an excellent exchange

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Apart from VERY unsatisfactory course selection proces, everything was fine at the international office was quite helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A mentor was offered.    Gave a little help regarding course selection.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Course selection horrible.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Not too difficult,  since I have been to Taiwan before, and I speak Chinese

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start early in yout search. Find a local partner if possible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty useless for mature students, but in Taibei oviousle quite a few possibiliies, although rather expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: International students were assigned a place and a short time interval (30 mins?)  and it went down easy with a few minute waiting time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: English speaking staff

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Half succesful.  Got good classes, but was enrolled on chinese litt., with the purpose of reading Taiwan litt.  That did not succeed at all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask for course selection help and advice from the Office of International Affairs.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Generelly very good, but to few litt classes

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Seminar on Asian Democratization on graduate level. College Chinese on graduate lever.  In all classes I had to pass with at least a B minus, because I was graduate, that was also the cass for undergraduate classes. So graduate students have to pass a higher barrier then undergraduates.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Good lectures.  As the best here. Language classes rather more formal than here. Could have used more language production - but wonderful that so many classes were in Chinese

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Asian Democratization .  Graduate Seminar
Taiwan Politics.  Lectures
University Chinese -  Course in Academic Chinese for Chinese speaking students from outside Taiwan
Advanced Chinese - 1. level advanced.
Extra Chinese classes .  2. level advanced

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Language Classes.

Courses on Taiwanese politics, society, history etc.

questions.answer: I bought a bicycle.  Cost 1200 kr., but I have taken it home on the plane at no cost

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports good opportunities. Culture more os less useless.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Meet people in Town.  Visit the same coffee house every day.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around the Island.  Everything can be reached in a weekend.  If you like mountain hiking the opportunies are good.   Taibei is at great exciting metropole, with plenty of cultural offerings, bars and great shops.  Bike rides along the river.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Second time on exchange in Taiwan so not to difficult. Taiwanese people are friendly and helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No.  I am a mature students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Taiwanese friendliness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
NTU is an ambitious elite university, so you are expected to work fairly hard.
Spend time in Taibei.  Travel the Island
Socialize with other exchange students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I had kind of a break through when it comes to writing Chinese. That was very tough and wonderful

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Writing essays and exams in chinese

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to Taiwan - it is a wonderful free Asian country.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
